newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-MIJATOVIC HELPS REAL TO RAIN-SOAKED VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MIJATOVIC HELPS REAL TO RAIN-SOAKED VICTORY.

text.p: Montenegrin striker Predrag Mijatovic cheered up Real Madrid fans drenched by a summer rainstorm in the Spanish capital by putting his side on the way to a comfortable 3-0 win over newly-promoted Hercules on Sunday.
The win left Real on four points, behind early leaders Tenerife, who along with Barcelona, Racing Santander and Real Sociedad each have six points after winning their first two games.
In matches played on Saturday, Barcelona beat Espanyol 2-1, title-holders Atletico Madrid crashed 3-1 to Compostela and Tenerife won 1-0 at Logrones.

Mijatovic, who was making his home league debut for Real after signing from Valencia, stretched superbly to a cross from Brazilian defender Roberto Carlos to find the net with a quarter of an hour on the clock.
Twenty minutes later Raul Gonzalez headed home the second, and the teenager made it three in a second half when the heavy rain made organised play virtually impossible.
The game marked the debut in Real colours of former German international keeper Bodo Illgner, who was scarcely troubled by the Hercules attack.

Sevilla's Argentine international defender Matias Almeyda had a less happy debut. His side became one of four teams not to have taken any points from their opening two games after losing 2-1 at home to Zaragoza.

Joining Sevilla at the bottom are Rayo Vallecano -- who lost 3-2 at Athletic Bilbao -- Espanyol and Valencia, both sides that had brought forward their games to Saturday ahead of UEFA Cup fixtures midweek.
Racing Santander's 1-0 victory at Sporting Gijon gives them a surprise 100 percent record, while Celta Vigo and Deportivo Coruna shared the points in a Galician derby which finished 1-1.
The second weekend of Spanish first division action will be completed with Real Betis' visit to Extremedura for Monday's televised match.
